long:
What makes krill oil different from fish oil?

Both krill oil and fish oil supply EPA and DHA — the two omega-3 fatty acids most studied for heart, brain, and joint health. The difference is in how those omega-3s are packaged. Standard fish oil delivers EPA and DHA as triglycerides. Krill oil delivers them as phospholipids, the same form that makes up cell membranes. Phospholipid-bound omega-3s are transported directly into cells, and several head-to-head comparisons suggest higher blood levels are achieved per dose compared with equivalent triglyceride fish oil.

Krill oil also contains astaxanthin — a carotenoid antioxidant that gives krill its red colour. Astaxanthin protects the delicate omega-3 fatty acids from oxidation in the bottle and, separately, has its own anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity in the body.

Inside each Jarrow Krill Oil softgel

  • 600 mg Antarctic krill oil — sourced from sustainably harvested Euphausia superba
  • 100 mg EPA and 60 mg DHA as phospholipid-bound omega-3 fatty acids
  • 1.5 mg natural astaxanthin per softgel
  • 60 mg phospholipids per serving
  • Small, easy-to-swallow softgels — no fishy repeat
  • 60 softgels per bottle, a 30-day supply at two per day

How to use

Take two softgels daily with a meal. Because krill oil omega-3s are delivered as phospholipids, absorption is less dependent on dietary fat compared with triglyceride fish oil, but taking it with food is still advisable to reduce the chance of digestive discomfort. Do not take if you have a shellfish allergy.

Jarrow Theanine 200

L-theanine is the amino acid responsible for the composed, unhurried alertness that distinguishes a cup of green tea from a cup of coffee. It doesn't suppress stimulation — it smooths it. At 200 mg, the dose Jarrow Formulas provides in each capsule, theanine has been shown in human trials to increase alpha-wave brain activity, which researchers associate with relaxed but engaged attention. Most people describe it as taking the edge off without taking away the focus.

The combination of theanine and caffeine is one of the most consistently validated pairings in the human performance literature. Theanine blunts the jitteriness and cardiovascular spike that caffeine alone can produce, while preserving and often extending the attention benefits. 200 mg theanine with 100 to 200 mg caffeine is a practical starting point for this effect.

Theanine also has a role independent of caffeine: taken at 200 to 400 mg before bed, it's associated with faster sleep onset and fewer nighttime awakenings in controlled research, likely through its activity on GABA and glutamate pathways. Unlike prescription sleep aids or over-the-counter antihistamine sleep products, it leaves no residual sedation the next morning.

Each bottle contains 60 vegetarian capsules — gluten-free, with no artificial additives. Capsule dosing is far more consistent than relying on theanine from tea, where concentrations vary by a factor of ten depending on the leaf grade and brew time. long:
Jarrow Glucosamine + Chondroitin + MSM

What does this supplement actually do?

Glucosamine, chondroitin, and MSM address joint health from three different directions. Glucosamine is a primary building block of cartilage and synovial fluid — the lubricant inside joints. Chondroitin supports the structural integrity of cartilage and may slow its enzymatic breakdown. MSM (methylsulfonylmethane) donates sulfur for connective tissue proteins and has its own track record for reducing joint discomfort and swelling in clinical trials. Combined, the three ingredients are the most widely studied nutritional joint-support stack.

What's in each capsule, and is the dose meaningful?

Each capsule provides 500 mg glucosamine hydrochloride, 400 mg sodium chondroitin sulfate, and 250 mg OptiMSM® — a pharmaceutical-grade, distillation-purified MSM. At three capsules per day (the label recommendation), you get 1,500 mg glucosamine, 1,200 mg chondroitin, and 750 mg MSM. Those are exactly the doses used in the major clinical trials on these ingredients, including the GAIT trial that studied glucosamine and chondroitin in participants with moderate-to-severe knee pain. Jarrow uses glucosamine HCl rather than glucosamine sulfate: HCl delivers more elemental glucosamine per gram and has equivalent research support.

How long before you notice a difference?

Joint supplements work slowly. Clinical studies typically run 12 to 24 weeks before assessing outcomes, and most participants report meaningful change in comfort and flexibility only after 8 to 12 weeks of consistent daily use. This is a maintenance supplement, not a painkiller — the mechanism is structural and gradual rather than immediate.

Who is it best suited for?

Adults who notice morning joint stiffness, reduced range of motion after activity, or age-related wear in the knees, hips, or hands. People with active lifestyles who want to support joint durability over time. It is not a treatment for acute injury or severe arthritis — consult a doctor if you have significant joint damage.
